comparisons.peer_topic: Bank Subsidiary Liquidity Sources and Constraints
comparisons.peer_summary: Bank subsidiary liquidity is driven by deposit and lending activities, securities valuation, and net debt activity, with additional incremental liquidity generated by pledging unencumbered loans and securities to FHLBs and the Federal Reserve Discount Window. The cash obtainable from borrowing against these eligible assets was $328 billion and $312 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, though regulatory restrictions generally limit the use of this liquidity to funding obligations within the bank subsidiaries.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose the fair value of unencumbered securities as a key liquidity source and note that borrowing against these assets provides incremental liquidity. However, JPM reports a total stock of $594 billion in unencumbered marketable securities at year-end 2024, which decreased from the prior year. In contrast, BAC reports a specific borrowing capacity of $328 billion derived from pledging unencumbered loans and securities at its bank subsidiaries at year-end 2024, an increase from $312 billion in 2023. BAC also highlights regulatory restrictions that generally limit the use of this liquidity to bank subsidiary obligations, whereas JPM notes that while some excess HQLA is non-transferable, the broader unencumbered securities are believed to be available to raise liquidity.

sentences.text: In addition to the assets reported in the Firm's eligible HQLA discussed above, the Firm had unencumbered marketable securities, such as equity and debt securities, that the Firm believes would be available to raise liquidity.

The fair value of these securities was approximately $594 billion and $649 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, although the amount of liquidity that could be raised at any particular time would be dependent on prevailing market conditions.

The decrease compared to December 31, 2023, was driven by reductions in unencumbered AFS securities in Treasury and CIO, excess eligible HQLA securities at JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., and unencumbered CIB trading assets.
Bank subsidiaries can also generate incremental liquidity by pledging a range of unencumbered loans and securities to certain FHLBs and the Federal Reserve Discount Window.
The cash we could have obtained by borrowing against this pool of specifically-identified eligible assets was $328 billion and $312 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023.

Due to regulatory restrictions, liquidity generated by the bank subsidiaries can generally be used only to fund obligations within the bank subsidiaries, and transfers to the Parent or nonbank subsidiaries may be subject to prior regulatory approval.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup had approximately $933 billion of available liquidity resources, consisting of $554 billion in end-of-period HQLA, $227 billion in additional unencumbered HQLA, and $152 billion in unused borrowing capacity from FHLB and Federal Reserve Bank discount windows.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose substantial reserves of unencumbered High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to support liquidity. JPM reports $594 billion in unencumbered marketable securities as of Dec 31, 2024, noting a decrease from $649 billion in 2023 driven by reductions in Treasury, CIO, and CIB assets. Citigroup reports a broader liquidity picture with $933 billion in total available resources, explicitly breaking out $227 billion in 'additional unencumbered HQLA' (excess liquidity at bank entities non-transferable to other entities). Both firms highlight that a portion of these unencumbered assets (JPM's excess HQLA and Citi's non-transferable excess liquidity) faces transferability constraints or are held at the bank entity level.

sentences.text: The fair value of these securities was approximately $594 billion and $649 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, although the amount of liquidity that could be raised at any particular time would be dependent on prevailing market conditions.

The decrease compared to December 31, 2023, was driven by reductions in unencumbered AFS securities in Treasury and CIO, excess eligible HQLA securities at JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., and unencumbered CIB trading assets.

As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup had approximately $933 billion of available liquidity resources to support client and business needs, including end-of-period HQLA ($554 billion); additional unencumbered HQLA, including excess liquidity held at bank entities that is non-transferable to other entities within Citigroup ($227 billion); and unused borrowing capacity from available assets not already accounted for within Citi's HQLA to support additional advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) and the Federal Reserve Bank discount window ($152 billion).

comparisons.peer_summary: In addition to the GCLA, the company holds other unencumbered assets including government obligations, money market securities, corporate obligations, equities, loans, and cash deposits, which are not considered liquid enough for GCLA eligibility. The fair value of these other unencumbered assets averaged $292.22 billion for the year ended December 2024, $281.95 billion for the year ended December 2023, $295.49 billion for the three months ended December 2024, and $286.51 billion for the three months ended December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS disclose holdings of unencumbered securities that are not part of their core eligible HQLA/GCLA metrics but serve as additional liquidity buffers. JPM reports $594 billion in unencumbered marketable securities (including excess HQLA) as of Dec 31, 2024. Goldman Sachs reports 'Other Unencumbered Assets' with an average fair value of $292.22 billion for the year ended Dec 2024, consisting of government obligations, corporate obligations, and equities. GS explicitly states these assets are not considered liquid enough for inclusion in their Global Core Liquidity Assets (GCLA), whereas JPM includes some of these assets (excess eligible HQLA) in its unencumbered securities count but notes they may be non-transferable to non-bank affiliates.

sentences.text: In addition to the assets reported in the Firm's eligible HQLA discussed above, the Firm had unencumbered marketable securities, such as equity and debt securities, that the Firm believes would be available to raise liquidity.
This includes excess eligible HQLA securities at JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. that are not transferable to non-bank affiliates.

In addition to our GCLA, we have a significant amount of other unencumbered cash and financial instruments, including other government obligations, high-grade money market securities, corporate obligations, marginable equities, loans and cash deposits not included in our GCLA.

The fair value of our unencumbered assets averaged $295.49 billion for the three months ended December 2024, $286.51 billion for the three months ended December 2023, $292.22 billion for the year ended December 2024 and $281.95 billion for the year ended December 2023.
We do not consider these assets liquid enough to be eligible for our GCLA.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and composition of HQLA held in subsidiaries
comparisons.peer_summary: High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) are presented prior to applying weightings and include all HQLA held in subsidiaries. The assets are primarily composed of unencumbered government obligations from France, the U.K., Japan, Italy, Germany, and Spain.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and MS discuss the composition and location of their high-quality liquid assets, specifically referencing government obligations held in subsidiaries. MS reports that its HQLA is primarily composed of unencumbered government obligations from specific countries (France, UK, Japan, etc.) and is held in subsidiaries. JPM reports a larger aggregate of unencumbered marketable securities ($594 billion) which includes excess eligible HQLA at JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., noting that some of these are not transferable to non-bank affiliates. While MS focuses on the geographical and institutional composition of HQLA in subsidiaries, JPM focuses on the total fair value and the trend of decrease in its broader unencumbered securities pool.
